nodes.text: Flow Matching (FM) is a simulation-free objective for training Continuous Normalizing Flows by regressing a neural vector field onto the vector field of a fixed target probability path, enabling CNF training at unprecedented scale.
nodes.evidence: Flow Matching (FM), a simulation-free approach for training CNFs based on regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths

nodes.text: Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) regresses onto per-sample conditional vector fields and provides an unbiased, tractable training objective that has identical gradients to the intractable marginal Flow Matching objective.
nodes.evidence: The FM (equation 5) and CFM (equation 9) objectives have identical gradients w.r.t. theta

nodes.text: A marginal vector field obtained by aggregating per-example conditional vector fields generates the corresponding marginal probability path, allowing the intractable marginal field to be decomposed into simple conditional fields (Theorem 1).
nodes.evidence: The marginal vector field (equation 8) generates the marginal probability path (equation 6)

nodes.text: Flow Matching is compatible with a general family of Gaussian probability paths that subsumes existing diffusion paths as specific instances, so one can work directly with probability paths without reasoning about diffusion processes.
nodes.evidence: compatible with a general family of Gaussian probability paths for transforming between noise and data samples—which subsumes existing diffusion paths as specific instances

nodes.text: Applying Flow Matching with diffusion paths gives a more robust and stable alternative to score matching for training diffusion models, achieving superior performance even on diffusion paths.
nodes.evidence: employing FM with diffusion paths results in a more robust and stable alternative for training diffusion models

nodes.text: Optimal Transport displacement interpolation defines conditional probability paths whose conditional vector field has constant direction in time and forms straight-line trajectories, unlike the curved trajectories of diffusion paths.
nodes.evidence: conditional OT paths are simpler than diffusion paths, forming straight line trajectories whereas diffusion paths result in curved paths... the OT path's conditional vector field has constant direction in time

nodes.text: Unlike diffusion-derived paths, which do not reach a true noise distribution in finite time and only approximate p0 by a Gaussian, the OT construction gives full control over the probability path by directly setting the mean and standard deviation.
nodes.evidence: as these probability paths were previously derived as solutions of diffusion processes, they do not actually reach a true noise distribution in finite time... our construction provides full control over the probability path

nodes.text: Existing simulation-free CNF training methods either involve intractable integrals or biased gradients, and maximum-likelihood CNF training requires expensive ODE simulations; Flow Matching breaks the barrier to scalable CNF training beyond diffusion.
nodes.evidence: existing simulation-free methods either involve intractable integrals (Rozen et al., 2021) or biased gradients (Ben-Hamu et al., 2022)... FM breaks the barriers for scalable CNF training beyond diffusion

nodes.text: For Gaussian conditional paths defined by time-dependent mean mu_t(x1) and std sigma_t(x1), there is a unique canonical vector field u_t(x|x1) = (sigma'_t/sigma_t)(x - mu_t) + mu'_t generating the path (Theorem 3).
nodes.evidence: the unique vector field that defines psi_t has the form: u_t(x|x1) = sigma_t'(x1)/sigma_t(x1) (x - mu_t(x1)) + mu'_t(x1)

nodes.text: Training CNFs with Flow Matching and OT paths on ImageNet consistently outperforms alternative diffusion-based methods in both likelihood and sample quality, and allows fast reliable sampling with off-the-shelf ODE solvers.
nodes.evidence: Training CNFs using Flow Matching on ImageNet leads to consistently better performance than alternative diffusion-based methods in terms of both likelihood and sample quality

nodes.text: OT paths provide better trade-offs between computational cost and sample quality than prior methods, translating empirically to faster training, faster generation, and better generalization.
nodes.evidence: These properties seem to empirically translate to faster training, faster generation, and better performance
